name: Bhee Patata
subtitle: rhizome and potato braised down in a dry onion-tomato masala until the edges catch

ingredients.note: sliced into coins; keep in water so it does not brown

prepNotes: Scrub the lotus stem hard before peeling — the hollow channels running through it trap river mud, and it is gritty if you skip this. Slice into 5mm coins.

Boil the lotus stem coins in salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife enters against slight resistance. It stays crisp however long you cook it, so do not wait for soft. Drain and dry them well — wet slices will never brown.
Cut the potato thick, in fingers rather than cubes, so it survives the long braise without disintegrating.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds, about 20 seconds.
Fry the par-boiled lotus stem coins and the potato fingers on medium-high for 8 minutes, turning once or twice, until patched with gold. Lift them out.
steps.tip: Do this in two batches if the pan is crowded. Steamed vegetables here mean a bland, pallid dish.

steps.text: In the same oil, fry the onion 8-10 minutes until properly brown at the edges, not merely soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute, until the raw garlic smell goes.
Stir in the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook 6-8 minutes, until the mass darkens and oil pools at the sides.
steps.tip: Wait for the oil to separate. This is the point at which the masala stops tasting of raw tomato.

steps.text: Return the vegetables, turn them through the masala, add the water and cover.
Cook on low 12-15 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the potato is tender and almost no liquid remains.
steps.tip: Stirring breaks the potato into mush. Shake and tilt the pan instead.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and let it fry dry for 2-3 minutes so the underside catches and crusts.
Sprinkle over the amchur and coriander leaves, toss once and take it off the heat.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat uncovered in a pan over medium heat so it crisps again rather than sweating — this is a dry dish and it suffers in the microwave.
